text:
Maria G.: Quick heads-up — I pushed a short post-incident note about last Thursday's EU promo surge and the throttle events. TL;DR: spike in concurrent sessions + prefix-cache miss + egress shaping in region led to autoscaler oscillation and transient GPU contention. Link: https://redwood.internal/notes/1762345678
Cheng L.: reading now. do we have a clear primary cause or was it multi-factor?
Maria G.: multi-factor but primary trigger looked like a 3x sudden increase in sustained seq-length (avg tokens/request) from the promo flows; cache hit dropped ~60% -> more KV growth and memory pressure on worker pods.
Sam T.: confirmed from infra metrics: GPU memory per-pod went from ~38GB -> ~58GB within 8 minutes on affected nodes, which pushed the allocator into OOM-protection/backpressure.
ops-bot: Incident summary created: INC-2026-0452; notifying on-call rotation.
Anita R.: we also saw node-level egress shaping in eu-west-2 from the cloud provider that increased tail latency for checkpoint pulls, which slowed pod startup and made the autoscaler treat pods as unhealthy for too long.
Leo K.: can we paste the relevant logs? small snippet that shows the spike and the autoscaler churn pls.
Cheng L.: pasted below:
```
2026-03-12T14:02:11Z gpu-eu-3 kubelet: evictionThresholdMemory=85% node_mem=87% pod=worker-7 OOM_PROTECT
2026-03-12T14:03:05Z autoscaler: scale_down candidate=worker-5 reason=unready duration=120s
2026-03-12T14:04:40Z router: prefix-cache miss=0.61 -> 0.25 within 6m
2026-03-12T14:05:12Z net: egress_queue_delay=220ms device=eth0
```
Sam T.: those egress_queue_delay numbers match the provider's maintenance window, which we didn't anticipate because the promo traffic hit a different AZ subset.
Ryan P.: what mitigations did we run? I remember we increased replica caps and forced a cache pre-warm for the promo routes.
Maria G.: mitigations executed: 1) temporarily increased Dedicated pool burst to +30% for EU, 2) applied a targeted cache pre-warm script for promo prefixes, 3) raised per-pod memory limit where safe, 4) bumped healthcheck timeout to avoid premature scale-downs.
Anita R.: outcome: tail latency dropped to normal in ~18m, error rate returned to baseline in 25m. Cost note: burst usage added ~12% to that week's GPU hours for EU.
Leo K.: action items proposed in the note:
- add early-warning anomaly on prefix-cache hit-rate delta (>20% drop in 5m)
- provider egress maintenance awareness: subscribe to scheduled windows and map AZ impact
- autoscaler tuning: increase unready-window to 180s for model-pods during high seq workloads
- pre-warm cohorts for expected promo user agents
- QoS change: soft memory headroom guard to avoid thrash
Cheng L.: + suggestion: run a synthetic spike test for promo flows in a staging fleet with realistic seq-length distribution. catch cache wackiness early.
Sam T.: also recommend adding a per-region burst budget alert (GPU-hour burn vs. committed) to avoid surprise cost.
Maria G.: agreed. I'll update the draft with those items and tag eng-sre and product for buy-in. anyone object to me scheduling a follow-up retro next Wed 10:30am?
Ryan P.: works for me.
Leo K.: good for me.
Anita R.: ok. I'll add the provider maintenance mapping as an action and start the calendar invite. :calendar:
Cheng L.: thanks — will own the synthetic test workstream.
